description: Dedicated to bridging planetary science and terrestrial exploration, our two-person core team leverages advanced web technology and geographical analysis to map Earth locations analogous to permanent Moon bases and Mars environments. Combining rigorous spatial research with rapid, data-driven prototyping, we deliver a streamlined solution for sustainable off-world habitation planning.
summary:
Vectorlab is an interactive, browser-based Planetary Analog Mapper designed to bridge terrestrial field research with future Lunar and Martian exploration. Built as a lightweight, zero-latency geospatial intelligence (GIS) dashboard, Vectorlab maps extreme Earth environments—the McMurdo Dry Valleys, Atacama Desert, Iceland’s volcanic lava tubes, Rio Tinto, and Devon Island’s Haughton Crater—that replicate the geological, mineralogical, and climatic conditions of the Moon and Mars.

Addressing the challenge of preparing mission hardware, rovers, and crews for extraterrestrial surfaces, Vectorlab enables researchers, students, and mission planners to filter analog testbeds by target celestial body and inspect comparative regolith compositions, environmental stressors, and space agency testing utility in real time. Because testing life-detection instruments, ice drills, and EVA habitats in space is prohibitively expensive, terrestrial analogs are vital for de-risking missions prior to launch. Vectorlab transforms complex planetary science data into an intuitive operational tool for exploration planning and STEM education.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

Vectorlab is an interactive Planetary Analog Geographic Information System (GIS) modeled after real aerospace mission-control telemetry consoles. Upon launch, users explore a dark-mode global map populated with custom pulsing telemetry beacons marking five scientifically verified terrestrial analog locations:

1. McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica (Mars Polar & Permafrost Analog)

2. Atacama Desert, Chile (Mars Regolith & Hyper-Aridity Analog)

3. Iceland Volcanic Fields & Lava Tubes (Moon & Mars Basalt/Subsurface Analog)

4. Rio Tinto, Spain (Mars Ancient Aqueous & Mineralogical Analog)

5. Devon Island / Haughton Crater, Canadian Arctic (Moon & Mars Impact Crater Analog)

Users can dynamically filter locations via the top navigation bar (ALL ANALOGS, MARS TARGETS, LUNAR TARGETS), monitor live cursor coordinates and UTC mission time, and click any beacon or directory card to smoothly fly to the coordinates and inspect a structured scientific briefing covering site summaries, mineralogical regolith breakdowns, extreme climate/radiation metrics, and space agency testing utility.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used:

- Frontend Architecture: HTML5, CSS3 (Glassmorphism UI, CSS keyframe radar animations, and custom dark-mode raster tile filters), and Vanilla ES6 JavaScript.

- Styling & Typography: Tailwind CSS, Google Fonts (Inter and JetBrains Mono), and Lucide open-source vector icons.

- Mapping & Geospatial Engine: Leaflet.js interactive mapping library paired with OpenStreetMap global tile layers.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered:

Rather than presenting planetary analog data as static text tables, our team designed Vectorlab as an intuitive mission-operations interface. Key engineering considerations included:

- Zero-Latency Portability: Engineered to run natively in any modern web browser without backend dependencies, CORS bottlenecks, or exposed API keys.

- Visual Target Differentiation: Color-coded pulsing markers distinguish Mars-specific analogs (amber beacons) from dual Moon & Mars testbeds (cyan beacons).

- Quantitative Scannability: Visual mineral composition progress bars (SiO2, Fe2O3, subsurface H2O ice, sulfates, and perchlorates) allow users to immediately compare terrestrial soil profiles against Lunar and Martian regolith.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

Before deploying rovers, subsurface ice drills, ground-penetrating radar, or astronaut habitats to the Moon and Mars, space agencies rely on Earth analogs to validate technology readiness. Vectorlab makes planetary analog research accessible to students, educators, and early-stage mission designers, illustrating how studying Earth’s extreme environments directly prepares humanity for sustainable off-world exploration.
